desc: A classic with very good imaging performance. This lens-type telezoom is quite manageable and lightweight despite an overall length of approx. 460 mm. User advantage: the mounted 360° rotatable tripod collar allows balanced attachment to a tripod and easy switching between portrait and landscape orientation. A close focus distance of about 5 m at the 1300 mm setting lets nature photographers select exciting subjects. On the vast majority of cameras the lens is used in shutter-priority or manual mode—see your camera manual for details. T2 mount, usage tip: screw the T2 adapter onto the lens, then lock the lens onto the camera. The small lateral screws on the T2 adapter, when loosened, allow you to tilt/align the lens—to bring the infinity index or depth-of-field marks upward. Re-tightening the screws secures lens and adapter reliably. Advantages of a full-frame lens on a camera with an APS-C sensor: save time in post-processing. Many lens defects such as distortion, edge softness or vignetting occur in the outer image areas. If you use a lens designed for full frame on a camera with an APS-C sensor, those outer areas are not used. This yields maximum quality and eliminates additional post-processing time to correct lens faults.
